first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, which is a direct signal that our previous success (memory_86: shortening onboarding improved completion) may be eroding due to changes elsewhere in the product or market. Simplifying onboarding aligns with memory_31 (cutting required fields produced durable activation lift) and memory_91 (activation messaging helps). I'm deliberately avoiding promotional_pricing despite competitive pressure because memory_73 shows it materially harms 30-day retention—winning price-sensitive SMBs with pricing cuts would damage long-term qualified revenue, our primary objective. I'm verifying memory_73 to confirm retention damage remains material, and memory_86 to understand the specifics of what 'shortening' meant before we experiment. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well but only with established customers, and we need to solve activation and onboarding first. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is higher-leverage but doesn't address the activation decline signal. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding targets the measurable drop directly, leverages proven mechanisms, and preserves the option to pivot if these results diverge from earlier findings.
